evidence: Gell. 4.5.5: malum cōnsilium cōnsultōrī pessimum est
terms.comment: Bad in every sense: bad weather, bad bread, a bad book, a bad man. Short a: mālus is the apple tree (Quint. 1.7.2). The adverb is male, badly (see not bad). A bad illness or wound is gravis; a child who is being bad is improbus (see naughty); for food that has gone bad, see bad (of food).

phrases.latin: dīcit vīlicus sēdulō sē fēcisse, servōs nōn valuisse, tempestātēs malās fuisse
phrases.english: the bailiff says he did his best, the slaves were ill, the weather was bad
‘Bad bread,’ you say. Wait: it will turn good.
